فَحِيلٌ : see فَحْلٌ, first sentence. ―
-b2- One says also فَحْلٌ فَحِيلٌ, meaning A generous stallioncamel, that begets generous offspring. (S, K. *) Er-Rá'ee says, “كَانَتْ نَجَائِبَ مُنْذِرٍ وَمُحَرِّقٍ
أُمَّاتُهُنَّ وَطَرْقُهُنَّ فَحِيلَا
” [Their mothers were of the generous camels of Mundhir and Moharrik, and their compressing stallion was a generous one, a begetter of generous offspring]: (S [accord. to one of my copies], and TA:) [some copies of the S have نَجَائِبُ and أُمَّاتِهِنّ; and so has the O: but] IB says that the verse is correctly related as above. (TA.) ―
-b3- And كَبْشٌ فَحِيلٌ means A ram that resembles the فَحْل of camels in his excellence (K, TA) and his [comparative] greatness. (TA.) ―
-b4- See also فَحْلٌ again, third sentence.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
